pull.title: feat: per-tier model fallback chains and a vision adapter model
pull.body:
## What this adds

Two related routing capabilities, both configurable from **Admin UI → Model Config**.

### Fallback chains

A single dead model took down a whole tier. If `MODEL_OPUS` pointed at a provider that was rate-limiting, out of credit, or had quietly retired the model id, every Opus request failed — even with three other providers configured and healthy.

Each tier now carries an ordered comma-separated list:

| Setting | Chain used |
| --- | --- |
| `MODEL_FALLBACKS` | after `MODEL`, for any tier with no override of its own |
| `MODEL_FABLE_FALLBACKS` | after `MODEL_FABLE` |
| `MODEL_OPUS_FALLBACKS` | after `MODEL_OPUS` |
| `MODEL_SONNET_FALLBACKS` | after `MODEL_SONNET` |
| `MODEL_HAIKU_FALLBACKS` | after `MODEL_HAIKU` |

A tier with its own primary override uses **only** its own chain; the two are never merged. So the models a route will try are exactly the primary plus the chain sitting next to it, with no hidden coupling to reason about.

### The commit boundary is the whole design

Attempts are tried in order until one produces its **first chunk**. Past that chunk the response is committed to the wire, so a later failure propagates rather than retrying on the next model — swapping models mid-stream would splice two different completions into one answer.

Preflight runs lazily, one attempt at a time, so a healthy primary never pays to validate a fallback it will not use. A plan with a single attempt behaves exactly as before, including raising synchronously when it fails, which preserves the caller's existing error surface.

Requests naming a provider and model directly (`open_router/…`) are never redirected — an explicit choice is answered as asked. A chain entry whose provider has left the registry is skipped with a warning rather than failing the route: a resilience feature must not become the outage.

### Vision adapter

`MODEL_VISION` serves image-carrying requests when the model a route picked is **known** not to accept images. Capability comes from what providers publish — OpenRouter-dialect `architecture.input_modalities`, models.dev `modalities.input`/`attachment` — threaded through `ProviderModelInfo.supports_vision`.

Unknown capability is deliberately left alone. Most providers publish no modality data at all, and diverting on silence would move traffic away from models that handle images perfectly well. Fallbacks known to be blind are dropped from a diverted chain: answering a question about an image it cannot see is worse than failing.

### Analytics follow the model that answered

The executor calls back into `RequestCapture.set_routing` on each attempt, so a request log row names the model that actually served it, not the one the route started from. Chain and vision entries also join `configured_chat_model_refs`, so their providers are discovered and warmed like any primary.

## A defect found by exercising the real API

Applying a chain persisted the raw submission verbatim, while `Settings` canonicalises on load. `.env` kept

```
MODEL_OPUS_FALLBACKS=" cerebras/qwen-3-coder-480b , groq/kimi-k2 ,cerebras/qwen-3-coder-480b "
```

while the value in effect was the trimmed, deduplicated one — two sources of truth with the visible one wrong. Normalization now happens per field type on the way in.

## Verification

Against a live server on a throwaway `HOME` (never the real `~/.fcc`):

```
$ curl -s :8137/admin/api/config | ...
MODEL                      model            value='nvidia_nim/nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b'
MODEL_FALLBACKS            model_chain      value=''
MODEL_FABLE                optional_model   value=''
MODEL_FABLE_FALLBACKS      model_chain      value=''
MODEL_OPUS                 optional_model   value=''
MODEL_OPUS_FALLBACKS       model_chain      value=''
MODEL_SONNET               optional_model   value=''
MODEL_SONNET_FALLBACKS     model_chain      value=''
MODEL_HAIKU                optional_model   value=''
MODEL_HAIKU_FALLBACKS      model_chain      value=''
MODEL_VISION               optional_model   value=''

$ # POST the messy value above, then:
$ grep MODEL_OPUS_FALLBACKS ~/.fcc/.env
MODEL_OPUS_FALLBACKS=cerebras/qwen-3-coder-480b,groq/kimi-k2
```

Tests — 18 new:

- **12 routing** — chain composition, tier isolation, direct requests never redirected, unknown providers skipped, duplicates dropped, reasoning inherited by every attempt, and all six vision cases.
- **6 execution** — including the one that matters: a failure **after** the first chunk propagates and the fallback provider is never called.

```
$ uv run ty check
All checks passed!

$ env -u ENABLE_WEB_SERVER_TOOLS -u EXA_API_KEY uv run pytest -q
6 failed, 3256 passed, 25 skipped in 144.56s
```

The 6 are the PowerShell installer tests, which never run on Linux CI. Note on the standing local baseline of 14: the other 8 are caused by a real `EXA_API_KEY` in this shell defeating `Settings()` isolation — confirmed by re-running that selection with `env -u EXA_API_KEY`, which gives **132 passed, 0 failed**. Nothing here is a regression.

Also confirmed after the live-server testing that the real `~/.fcc/.env` (Aug 3) and `requests.db` were untouched and no state file was created there.

## Residual risks

- **No live request has been made through a chain against a real provider.** The failover logic is verified with provider doubles; a real 429-then-succeed round trip is not covered.
- **No model's vision metadata has been checked against a live `/models` payload.** The extractors are verified against the published response shapes and fixtures only. If a gateway spells `input_modalities` differently, that model reads as unknown and is simply left alone — the safe direction.
- **The chain editor has not been driven in a browser.** Rendering, reordering and the dirty-state hookup are verified by reading the apply path and by the API round-trip above, not by clicking it.
- Fallbacks multiply upstream attempts: each entry carries the provider's own retry behaviour, so a 4-long chain can quadruple worst-case attempts on a fully-broken configuration. Chains are opt-in and empty by default.

commit.message:
feat(routing): per-tier fallback chains and a vision adapter model

A single dead model took down a whole tier. If MODEL_OPUS pointed at a
provider that was rate-limiting, out of credit, or had quietly retired the
model id, every Opus request failed — even with three other providers
configured and healthy. There was no way to say "try this, then that".

Two related routing capabilities:

Fallback chains. Each tier gains a comma-separated ordered list
(MODEL_FALLBACKS, MODEL_{FABLE,OPUS,SONNET,HAIKU}_FALLBACKS). A tier with
its own primary override uses only its own chain; a tier without one uses
MODEL then MODEL_FALLBACKS. The two are never merged, so the models a route
will try are exactly the primary plus the chain sitting next to it — no
hidden coupling to reason about.

The mechanism is a RoutedMessagesPlan carrying ordered attempts, tried until
one produces its first chunk. That boundary is the whole design: past the
first chunk the response is committed to the wire, so a later failure
propagates rather than retrying on the next model. Swapping models mid-stream
would splice two different completions into one answer. Preflight runs lazily
one attempt at a time, so a healthy primary never pays to validate a fallback
it will not use, and a plan with a single attempt behaves exactly as before —
including raising synchronously when it fails, preserving the caller's error
surface.

Requests naming a provider and model directly are never redirected; an
explicit choice is answered as asked. A chain entry whose provider has left
the registry is skipped with a warning rather than failing the route — a
resilience feature must not become the outage.

Vision adapter. MODEL_VISION serves image-carrying requests when the model a
route picked is KNOWN not to accept images. Capability is read from what
providers publish (OpenRouter-dialect `architecture.input_modalities`,
models.dev `modalities.input`/`attachment`) and threaded through
ProviderModelInfo.supports_vision to a lookup on the request runtime. Unknown
capability is deliberately left alone: most providers publish no modality
data, and diverting on silence would move traffic away from models that
handle images perfectly well. Fallbacks known to be blind are dropped from a
diverted chain — answering about an image it cannot see is worse than
failing.

Analytics follow the model that answered, not the one the route started from:
the executor calls back into RequestCapture.set_routing on each attempt.
Fallback and vision entries also join configured_chat_model_refs so their
providers are discovered and warmed like any primary.

Verification:
- 12 new routing tests (chain composition, tier isolation, direct requests,
  unknown providers, duplicates, reasoning inheritance, all six vision cases)
- 6 new execution tests, including the one that matters: a failure AFTER the
  first chunk is propagated and the fallback provider is never called
- Full suite: 14 failed, 3236 passed — identical to the documented baseline on
  unmodified main (8 from a real EXA_API_KEY in the shell defeating Settings
  isolation, 6 PowerShell installer tests). Confirmed by re-running the
  websearch selection with `env -u EXA_API_KEY`: 132 passed, 0 failed.
- ruff format, ruff check, ty check all clean.

Not done: no live request has been made through a chain against a real
provider, and no model's vision metadata has been checked against a live
/models payload — both are verified against fixtures and the published
response shapes only.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(admin): fallback chain editor and canonical chain persistence

Adds the Model Routing UI for the chains added in the previous commit, plus a
defect found by exercising the real admin API rather than reading the code.

The editor renders a `model_chain` field as numbered rows, each reusing the
existing ModelCombobox so chain entries get the same model search as the
primary model fields. Rows move up/down (priority is the whole point of the
feature, so the order has to be visible and changeable) and remove. The wire
value stays a single comma-joined string in a hidden input carrying the usual
data-key/data-original, so the dirty-state and apply paths needed no changes
at all; row inputs deliberately carry no data-key or they would be collected
as settings in their own right.

The defect: applying a chain persisted the raw submission verbatim. Settings
canonicalises a chain when it loads it, so `.env` kept

    MODEL_OPUS_FALLBACKS=" cerebras/qwen-3-coder-480b , groq/kimi-k2 ,cerebras/qwen-3-coder-480b "

while the value actually in effect was the trimmed, deduplicated one. The
dashboard would have shown a string that differed from what was running --
two sources of truth, with the visible one wrong. Normalization now happens
per field type on the way in, so stored and effective are the same string.

Verification, against a live server on a throwaway HOME (never the real
~/.fcc):
- GET /admin/api/config returns all five chain fields as type `model_chain`,
  each ordered directly after the model it backs, plus MODEL_VISION.
- POST /admin/api/config/apply with the messy value above now persists
  `MODEL_OPUS_FALLBACKS=cerebras/qwen-3-coder-480b,groq/kimi-k2` -- whitespace
  trimmed, duplicate dropped, no quoting.
- Confirmed afterwards that the user's real ~/.fcc/.env and requests.db were
  untouched and no state file was created there.
- node --check on admin.js; ruff format, ruff check, ty check clean;
  tests/application 98 passed.

Not verified: the chain editor has not been driven in a browser. Rendering,
reordering and the dirty-state hookup are verified by reading the apply path
and by the round-trip above, not by clicking it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
